mechanism_narrative: Transit and workplace mobility have improved in each of the last two weekly prints, and this commuting restoration mechanically restores weekday trip chains that end in retail-and-recreation stops, so RETAIL_REC keeps climbing and its next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -68.9 to -64.7 across the last three weekly prints
fact:WORKPLACES rose from -62.4 to -60.4 over the same window
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has already slipped from 41.1 to 38.7 as containment fatigue sets in; once the weekly residential mean breaches 38.0, households shift a measurable share of trips out of the home and into discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
regime_hint: lockdown fatigue with restrictions still nominally in force
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls below 38.0, the following two-week mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the two-week mean preceding the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has stabilized near -21 while transit recovers, and only the joint occurrence of replenishment-stable supply and restored transit access converts into discretionary retail trips; transit recovery alone or grocery stability alone is insufficient.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 2 points week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM remains above -26
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -25.4 to -20.7 and held at -20.7 while TRANSIT rose from -70.1 to -64.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks in periods where both conditions hold, or rises equally often when only one of the two conditions holds.

mechanism_narrative: The mechanism is conditional on formal easing: once the stay-at-home order is replaced by a phased reopening that permits non-essential retail with capacity caps, workplace mobility converts into retail footfall with a four-week lag, because store reopenings follow policy announcements by roughly two to three weeks.
candidate_trigger: stay-at-home order replaced by a phased reopening order permitting non-essential retail
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -60.4 remains 60 points below baseline, indicating policy still binding
regime_hint: phased reopening with retail capacity caps
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is flat or lower than its last-28-day mean in the four weeks following a formal phased-reopening order, despite WORKPLACES continuing to recover.

mechanism_narrative: Households have shifted a persistent share of spending to grocery and pharmacy channels, which remain 21 points below baseline but far above the retail-and-recreation collapse; as long as grocery activity stays elevated above -25, trip budgets and wallet share stay allocated to essentials and discretionary retail recovery is capped or reversed.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above -25 for two consecutive weekly prints
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -25.4 to -20.7 while RETAIL_REC remained near -64
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds its last-28-day mean in periods when GROCERY_PHARM stays above -25 for two consecutive weeks, indicating no substitution drag.

mechanism_narrative: Late-May warming pulls discretionary out-of-home time into parks rather than indoor retail, so whenever park mobility improves by 3 points or more week-on-week, the freed trip volume substitutes away from retail-and-recreation venues and RETAIL_REC's four-week mean fails to beat its prior four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by at least 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -68.1 (t-2w) to -63.9 (t-0w), a 4.2-point rebound
regime_hint: late-spring warming with outdoor options open
failure_condition: Weeks with a PARKS improvement of at least 3 points are followed by RETAIL_REC gains at least as large as weeks with flat or falling PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: The binding constraint on retail is simultaneous un-sticking of home and work: when RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises in the same week, households resume dual out-of-home routines and the retail uptick appears within one week rather than with a lag.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises in the same weekly print
evidence_refs: fact:in the t-0w print RESIDENTIAL fell from 40.6 to 38.7 while WORKPLACES rose from -64.7 to -60.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the one to two weeks following weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises simultaneously, or the combination performs no better than either series alone.

mechanism_narrative: A stalled transit recovery while retail remains more than 60 points below baseline signals that authorities re-impose containment measures pre-emptively, and that policy reversal forces the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC below its last-28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change is zero or negative while RETAIL_REC is below -60
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at -63.9 and TRANSIT at -64.7 both remain more than 60 points below baseline
regime_hint: pre-emptive re-tightening triggered by stalled mobility recovery
failure_condition: Following a week where TRANSIT is flat or falling while RETAIL_REC is below -60, RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is higher than its last-28-day mean in the majority of instances.
